hook.text: A project has thousands of tasks — but only one sequence determines when it finishes.

buildup.text: CPM maps every task, its duration, and its dependencies — which tasks must finish before others start.

discovery.text: The longest chain of dependent tasks is the critical path — delay any one and the project is late.

twist.text: Non-critical tasks have float — they can slip without affecting the finish date.

climax.text: CPM was invented for the Polaris missile program — scheduling 3,000 contractors simultaneously.

punchline.text: Find the longest path and shorten it. That's how you finish a project faster.

quiz.question: What defines the critical path in a construction schedule?
options: The tasks that cost the most money to complete
The longest chain of dependent tasks that determines the project's minimum duration
The tasks assigned to the most experienced workers

details.summary: The Critical Path Method identifies the longest sequence of dependent activities in a project schedule, determining the shortest possible project duration. Any delay to a critical path activity directly delays the project completion date, while non-critical activities have float time available.
details.whyItMatters: CPM enables managers to focus resources on activities that actually control the finish date. Without identifying the critical path, teams may waste effort accelerating activities that have no impact on completion.
takeaways: The critical path is the longest chain of dependent activities through the network
Delays to critical activities delay the entire project by the same amount
Non-critical activities have float, meaning they can slip without affecting completion

faq.question: How is the critical path calculated in a project schedule?
faq.answer: A forward pass calculates the earliest start and finish for each activity. A backward pass calculates the latest start and finish without delaying the project. Activities where earliest and latest times are equal have zero float and form the critical path.

faq.question: Can a project have more than one critical path?
faq.answer: Yes. Multiple paths through the network can have the same longest duration. Near-critical paths with very little float are equally important to monitor because small delays can shift them onto the critical path. Some complex projects have dozens of near-critical paths.
